text:
mira: Proposal — require a signed header for any header-derived workspace routing on private endpoints + dedicated pools. If X-Workspace-Signature is missing/invalid, ignore the header and fall back to token/VPC binding. This avoids accidental tenant escape from misconfigured clients.

devin: +1 on safety. How do you envision signature validation? shared KMS key per customer? public-key per workspace?

mira: thinking public-key per workspace stored in control plane (customer publishes pubkey during onboarding). validation done at gateway routing layer before any routing decision. cheap crypto check, memoize for 5m.

sana: console-team asked for a toggle: "tenant-lock enforcement" on workspace settings so orgs can opt-in to strict header signing immediately. also want a dry-run mode that emits telemetry but doesn't block.

ryan: quota gotcha — if we accept header-derived workspace for a dedicated pool, we need to guard that quotas/committed capacity are enforced against the resolved workspace. race with autoscaler if we suddenly shift traffic to private pool that is low on capacity. suggest a pre-check: if dedicated_pool.available_compute < threshold then reject header-derived routing and fallback.

mira: agree. fallback rules: 1) if signature invalid -> fallback to token/VPC, 2) if target pool lacks capacity -> fallback to best-effort hosted or stall + 429 depending on customer policy. we should make this behavior configurable per workspace.

devin: can we emit clear telemetry so we can track how often header-derived routing was accepted vs rejected? proposed metrics: routing.scope_accept, routing.scope_reject_signature, routing.scope_reject_capacity, routing.scope_fallback_target. Also tag with pool_type and workspace_id (or hashed id).

sana: add console dashboards: percentage accepted over last 24h, top callers by client_id, and a small alert when scope_reject_capacity > 0.5% of requests for a workspace over 10m.

console-team: UX notes — for the toggle we should show a migration path: Dry-run (emit events) -> Enforce (block) -> Enforce + Auto-fallback to hosted (with opt-out). show a clear audit log for decisions with reason code.

mira: draft of gateway rule for review:
```
match: host: private.example.com
extract: header X-Workspace-Id, X-Workspace-Signature
validate: signature with workspace.pubkey
route_priority: [dedicated_pool_if_valid, token_binding, vpc_binding, hosted_fallback]
quota_check: enforce resolved_workspace.quota before accepting route
telemetry: emit routing.scope_accept|reject_* with tags: reason,pool,client_id
```

devin: nit — include a short TTL for memoized pubkeys and expose an invalidation hook when customer rotates keys. also consider verifying signature only for requests that request high QPS or dedicated pool, to save CPU for low-risk traffic.

ryan: rollout plan suggestion: canary to 1% of private endpoint traffic (dedicated pools) in dry-run mode for 48h, then 5% enforce with auto-fallback to hosted for 24h, then full enforce for orgs that opt-in. Need dashboards + alerting before step 2.

infra-bot: scheduled deploy: gateway/routing/signature-checker -> canary group A (1%) at 2026-04-02T02:00Z if approved.

deploy-bot: preview link: https://deploys.internal/2199998888-canary-signcheck (contains rollout plan + metric dashboard links).

sana: assigning follow-ups: mira to PR gateway rule, console-team to add toggle + audit UI, devex to update onboarding docs for pubkey upload, ryan to add capacity pre-check and quota gating. I'll create a ticket for dashboards/alerts.

mira: thanks — i'll open the gateway PR and add unit tests for signature validation + a small perf microbenchmark. will ping when ready for review. :thumbsup:

devin: thanks all, agree this reduces surface for header abuse without breaking existing token/VPC bindings.

ryan: fine to proceed with the canary schedule once the dashboards exist.

mira: marking this thread resolved for now, will post PR link.

infra-bot: thread status -> resolved
